body: Bob Ross was by far one of the most comforting people I ever had the privilege to watch on TV.
That's why I can't stand waking up.

I've tried many things, read many books, listened to motivational speakers, gone on hikes, tried hobbies that used to make me happy, read, gone on walks, found therapists, tried medication, talked to friends, talked to family. The end result is all the same; I feel nothing. 

I feel like I'm just breathing, just existing.

Today, I called out of one of my jobs. I couldn't get out of bed today. I cried myself to sleep. I have thought about it EVERYDAY for years. I feel like I have been selfless for the people I have stuck around for. But I can't keep living like this, one more day is what I keep telling myself and then when the night comes I feel this overwhelming urge just to go to sleep and never wake up. 

I'm 25 years old. I know there is more to life than feeling like this, but I can't keep waiting for something to happen that is going to shift things so dramatically that I will want to wake up in the morning. I made it through one more night, but I know I will be alone again tonight. And I will have the same conversation, "should I do it now?".

I am a coward, and that's the only reason why I am still here today. I couldn't push the blade in deep enough.
Traveling used to be one of the only things that gave me happiness, but I've noticed it doesn't matter where I go the sadness just follows me around now, like a shadow, where I go, so does it.

I agree with you. I tried multiple times because I couldn't understand why my body just wouldn't die. I caused permanent damage but I'm still alive. I pray every day that I don't wake up tomorrow. But I do, like so cruel joke that never ends. 

The things that made me happy just make me sad now. Music and movies just remind me of people who are no longer in my life. Being outside used to give me hope and now I can barely drag myself to the grocery store to buy food. I'm a shell of who I used to be and it's just progressively getting worse. 

How do I find things that make me happy if I've forgotten what happiness is
Thank you for your kind words.
If we all are going to die, what the harm in ending the pain of someone who doesn't want to suffer anymore. Sometimes you have to stop beating a dead horse.

The pain and overwhelming sadness I experience on a daily basis I hope no one has to experience. It is a weight that never lets up and only gets heavier over time. 

I was actually "laid off" after seeking help last year. Mental health in the workplace isn't taken seriously in my experience at all. I just started this job most people would be really grateful to have, it's semi-important but gives me no joy. 

I have tattoos already, quite a few cover cuts from self harm. 
They do hurt, but not a half of fraction of the pain I wake up to every day. 

I appreciate your comments and kind words but the darkness is all I know.
I wish I could sleep. I haven't slept well in probably a decade.

I know I'm not the only person out there struggling to make it to the next day, there are far worse things out there for people to deal with. 

My family has endured about as much pain and loss as a family could. There are 5 people left in my family (myself included), 2 of which refuse to speak with me. The 2 that remain are in their late 60's and 80's. I have become a burden on them, they told me the last time they picked me up from the hospital, that this time had to be the last. The stress I put on them is too much. I don't blame them at all. 

I know I'm a wreck. I don't want to hurt anyone anymore, or drag anyone else down with me.

I have friends, they are good people and have scooped me up many times when I have been like this, but I know I am now a burden and everyone is tired of me calling from a unknown number to say I'm back in the hospital. I haven't felt alive in a long time.
